item.title: Google launches Project Suncatcher, a step towards AI data centers in space
item.description: The fridge-size satellite with AI chips on board is part of Project Suncatcher, the company's moonshot effort to put AI data centers in space and harness solar energy.

item.title: A judge permanently dismisses former Olympian's Reflecting Pool charges
item.description: Citing "exceptional circumstances," a D.C. judge has ruled that the federal government cannot refile its Reflecting Pool charges against David Hearn, despite pressure from President Trump to do so.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: AI data centers: How much are ratepayers on the hook for?
item.description: Data centers consume large amounts of power and require upgrading infrastructure. But it's difficult to determine how much residential customers benefit and how much they actually pay for the benefit.

item.title: Cornell Jane Doe's attorney says she told police in 2024: 'I was raped'
item.description: Counter to what a local prosecutor has claimed, the alleged victim of a 2024 gang rape at Cornell University clearly said in her police statement that she was sexually assaulted, her attorney told NPR.

item.title: New space station crew launches from Florida on SpaceX's Crew Dragon capsule
item.description: The crew of four — two NASA astronauts, one from Canada, and a Russian cosmonaut — heads to the International Space Station after liftoff from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

item.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
item.description: In mother-of-pearl suits, the Pearly Kings used to canvass East London for charity. The most famous one, George Major, died in August. A look back on this larger-than-life figure and the Pearly King tradition.

item.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
item.description: President Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.

item.title: COMIC: How the census gives your state power (and what Trump wants to change)
item.description: The census is used to determine how much say your state has in Congress and the Electoral College. President Trump failed to alter it during his first term, but he's trying again ahead of 2030.
